text:
IncidentBot: Paging oncall — P1: EU generation latency spike affecting streaming responses on /v1/generate. Alert group: >5xx and p99 token latency >2s for 10+ minutes. Pager link: https://pager.example/INC-3281 :rotating_light:
Maya K: acked, paging in. I'm oncall — joining now.
Samir B: jumping in. I see a spike in 503s from gateway -> model-proxy in eu-west-1. logs: `2026-03-15T09:01:23Z ERROR proxy request failed code=503 conn=reset` repeated.
Li Chen: noticed autoscaler churn around the same time — several workers terminated then recreated. p95 latency went from ~120ms -> 2.4s.
Maya K: can someone check warm pool count and recent scale events? `kubectl get hpa --namespace=redwood` and `kubectl describe nodepool eu-gen`
Samir B: running quick query, past 15m: `count(status=503) by instance` shows 12 hosts with bursts. Also seeing KV cache misses for prefix caching: `kv_cache_miss_rate` jumped to 38%.
Ops Lead: if autoscaler removed warm workers on a spike we need to pin minReplicas while we mitigate. Set minReplicas=4 for model-svc-eu.
Maya K: doing it now: `kubectl scale deploy/model-svc-eu --replicas=4` — applied. Confirming rollout.
Julien R: adding temporary routing fallback to smaller model variant to relieve load: route policy set to prefer model-x-small on spike >1s latency. Applying traffic rule.
Samir B: ok we've reduced 503s by ~60% in the last 3m. p99 still high but trending down from 2.6s -> 1.1s.
Li Chen: drafting status update for customers — short + actionable. Posting draft below for review.
Li Chen: DRAFT (status page): "We are experiencing elevated latency and intermittent errors for streaming generation requests in our EU region. Engineers are investigating and mitigation actions (scaling and routing changes) are in progress. Impact: some requests may be delayed or receive 5xx errors. We will provide updates every 30 minutes."
Maya K: concise, add ETA for next update + note about SDK retry guidance. Suggest: "Next update in 30 minutes. Recommended: clients retry transient failures with exponential backoff."
Li Chen: updated DRAFT: "We are investigating elevated latency and intermittent 5xx errors impacting streaming generation in EU. Mitigations (scaling and routing changes) are underway. Some requests may be delayed or receive errors. Next update in 30 minutes. If you are on Dedicated capacity, please contact support for instance-level diagnostics"
StatusPage Bot: queued draft to staging. Review URL: https://status-staging.example/incidents/2164501234-preview
Maya K: internal comms template for IR channel (copyable):
```
Short summary: EU streaming generation latency spike, intermittent 5xx.
Impact: customers in EU may see delayed or failed generation responses.
Cause: under investigation (suspected autoscaler scale-down + cache churn).
Mitigation: increased min replicas, temporary routing to smaller model variant, monitoring.
Next update: in 30 minutes.
Owner(s): Maya K (oncall), Samir B (runtime), Li Chen (comms)
```
Samir B: digging deeper — root cause hypothesis: recent autoscaler scaling policy mis-evaluated warm-worker CPU metric during burst and removed instances; combined with cache invalidation caused higher cold-start work. We should look at the autoscaler window config `scaleDownDelaySeconds` and the warm pool target.
Ops Lead: filing a follow-up ticket to adjust scale down policy and add a prewarm probe. Assigning to eng-runtime. Ticket: ENG-7124.
Maya K: quick ask — anyone seen related deploys in last 30m? `deploy-bot`?
IncidentBot: Deploy detected: service=model-proxy, commit=ab3f9e2, env=eu, started=2026-03-15T08:52:10Z by samirb — no rollback.
Maya K: deploy timing is close to start of spike. Correlating. Samir, can you sanity-check proxy change?
Samir B: looking at proxy diff — small connection pooling tweak. Not likely the sole cause but may have amplified cold starts under churn. Rolling back not yet — prefer increase replicas + route fallback.
Li Chen: customer email draft for affected customers (short):
"We are currently experiencing elevated latency and intermittent errors for streaming generation in our EU region. Our engineers are actively mitigating the issue by increasing capacity and routing traffic to compatible model variants. We expect service to continue improving over the next hour. No action required from customers; if you depend on strict latency SLAs, please reach out to your account team. We will send another update in 30 minutes."
Julien R: looks good. Add: "If you see persistent errors, include request IDs and timestamps for faster triage."
Maya K: operational checklist for next 30m: monitor p95/p99, watch 5xx counts, keep minReplicas=4, confirm routing rule is stable, evaluate rollback if regressions.
Samir B: metrics now: 5xx count down 70%, p99 at 900ms. KV cache miss rate falling to 12%.
Li Chen: publishing initial status page update now per approval.
StatusPage Bot: Published update to status page (staging -> prod) at 2026-03-15T09:13Z by Li Chen. URL: https://status.example/incidents/2164501234
Maya K: great. continuing monitoring. If we hit regression revert to two-phase: rollback proxy change or scale further.
Ops Lead: pre-emptive follow-up action: create runbook task to add warm pool metric alarms and set minReplica guard for model deploys. ENG-7125 created.
Samir B: confirm we have logs for affected request IDs? I'm collecting trace bundle: `s3://traces/2164501234/`
Maya K: next update in 30 minutes unless resolved earlier.
--- 27 minutes later ---
Samir B: update: p99 ~420ms, 5xx negligible. Autoscaler parameters changed: `scaleDownDelaySeconds` increased from 60 -> 300. Warm pool min set to 3.
Li Chen: drafting resolved notice. DRAFT (status page resolved): "At 09:40 UTC we resolved elevated latency and intermittent errors affecting streaming generation in EU. Mitigations included increasing replica minimums, applying temporary routing to a smaller model variant, and adjusting autoscaler scale-down settings. Root cause under post-incident review. If you continue to see issues, contact support with request IDs."
Maya K: LGTM. Publish resolved.
StatusPage Bot: Resolved notice published at 2026-03-15T09:41Z by Li Chen.https://status.example/incidents/2164501234#resolved
Julien R: filing RCA owners: eng-runtime (Samir), infra (Ops Lead), comms (Li). Rough timeline and follow-ups in ENG-7124 / ENG-7125.
Maya K: handing off to next oncall (Julien R) for post-mortem and follow-ups. Handoff notes: replicas pinned, autoscaler changes applied, traces collected at s3 path above, follow-up tickets created.
Julien R: taking it. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
